lenses.title: Correctness
lenses.question: Does the change do what the PR says, for every input and state it can reach?
lenses.focus: Trace changed behaviour from entry point to persisted result. Look for wrong branches, off-by-one, missed states, broken invariants, and callers the diff forgot.

lenses.title: Security and privacy
lenses.question: Can anyone read, write or trigger something they should not?
lenses.focus: Authorization on every read and write, trust boundaries, injection, secrets in logs or responses, data sent to third parties, and endpoints newly reachable from a browser.

lenses.title: Durability and recovery
lenses.question: Does data survive crashes, retries, restarts and partial failure without loss or duplication?
lenses.focus: Idempotency, retries, lost updates, migrations, local or device storage, and what a user sees after a failure. Demand a reproduction for any loss claim.

lenses.title: Concurrency and races
lenses.question: What breaks when two actors, tabs, requests or timers interleave?
lenses.focus: Shared mutable state, stale responses applied after the context changed, check-then-act gaps, in-flight work across navigation, and ordering assumptions.

lenses.title: Errors and evidence
lenses.question: When something fails, does the user get a truthful message and the operator a usable diagnostic?
lenses.focus: Swallowed errors, generic messages that hide the cause, errors that leak internals, and failures reported as success.

lenses.title: Test quality
lenses.question: Would the tests fail if the change were reverted or broken, and do they test behaviour rather than implementation?
lenses.focus: Run the changed tests. Remove each protection the diff adds, one at a time, and report which removals no test catches. Flag tests that mirror implementation, assert trivia or rely on timing.

lenses.title: Simplicity
lenses.question: Is this the smallest change that solves the problem, without speculative layers?
lenses.focus: Unneeded abstractions, one-caller wrappers, configuration nobody asked for, dead code, and band-aid guards where a root-cause fix belongs.

lenses.title: Duplication and reuse
lenses.question: Does the change re-implement something the codebase or platform already provides?
lenses.focus: Hand-rolled helpers, parallel code paths, copied logic that will drift, and new mechanisms where an existing one fits.

lenses.title: Interface and experience
lenses.question: Is the user-facing behaviour clear, accessible and consistent with the rest of the product?
lenses.focus: Loading, empty, error and recovery states; keyboard and screen-reader access; mobile layout; copy that matches behaviour. Mark not relevant when no user surface changes.

lenses.title: Claims and documentation
lenses.question: Are the PR description, docs and evidence accurate about what was verified?
lenses.focus: Overstated verification, stale docs, evidence recorded for a different commit, and limitations left out.

lenses.title: Real integration
lenses.question: Has the change been exercised against the real dependency it relies on, not only fakes?
lenses.focus: Providers, databases, queues and external APIs. Name what was mocked, what a bounded real check would need, and its cost. Mark not relevant when no external dependency changes.
